Title: 3D Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click once on the Pattern segment to establish the first half of the seam. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. Note When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Segment Sewing. Note: 3D Sewing Video
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to effortlessly create Sewing Lines on patterns and shapes within a 3D environment, ensuring a seamless sewing operation across both 2D and 3D views.

Title: 3D M:N Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. Location Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing Note: Hold down the Segment Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Segment Sewing tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. Note: While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. Note: 3D Sewing Video
ContentDescription: "Streamline your sewing process by easily connecting and editing multiple segments in both 2D and 3D views with our M:N Segment Sewing tool."

Title: 1:N Free Sewing (2D)
Content: Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern (ver2.2.0). Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Establish the start and the end point on the Pattern outline, which is called as 1, where multiple Patterns are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Line appears in neon color. While holding down the Shift key, establish Sewing Lines on N Patterns. Similar to setting regular Free Sewing Lines, be careful with Directional Notches. Release the Shift key to complete. Note The difference in lengths between the first and second half seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it turns red to alert the user. While establishing 1:N Sewing Lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.
ContentDescription: "Learn how to efficiently establish and manage Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes to seamlessly combine multiple Patterns into a single design using the Free Sewing feature in our 2D Toolbar."

Title: Free Sewing (2D)
Content: Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Click, drag and click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. Note: The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. When establishing the second half of the seam, difference in the Sewing Line lengths appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. If the difference exceeds 1 inch, the difference appears in red to alert the user. Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to freely establish sewing lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes, utilizing the 2D toolbar to enhance their sewing projects with precision and ease.

Title: 1:N Segment Sewing (2D)
Content: Objective Easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. Note The difference in lengths between the first and second half seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it turns red to alert the user. While establishing 1:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the sewing line cannot be applied. While establishing N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for efficiently sewing multiple segments to a single segment while ensuring accurate alignment and length adjustments.

Title: Sewing Line Type
Content: Objective Apply the Turned Sewing Line type setting to achieve a folded, two ply look. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor Sewing Line Type 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor Sewing Line Type Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor Sewing Line Type 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing (Select Sewing Line) Property Editor Sewing Line Type Select Turned. Activate Simulation. Double layered Patterns are sewn together crisp and flat.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying the Turned Sewing Line type setting to create a folded, two-ply look in sewing projects.

Title: Show/Hide Sewing
Content: Objective When Sewing Lines are too complicated, hide them for clear view as needed. Location 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Show Sewing (All) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Show Sewing (All) The selected Sewing Lines or all Sewing Lines show or disappear from the 2D and the 3D window.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for using the 2D/3D Toolbar to hide or show sewing lines for improved visibility during complex sewing tasks.

Title: 3D Seamline
Content: Objective Adjust Intensity and Thickness of 3D seamlines to render a realistic Garment. Location Select Sewing Line Property Editor 3D Seamline Operation Select the Edit Sewing tool from the 2D/3D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Sewing Line Property Editor 3D Seamline Adjust the settings below as needed: Option Description Normal Map Intensity (%) Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. Thickness Adjust the thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the intensity and thickness of 3D seamlines to achieve realistic garment rendering in fashion design software.

Title: Select/Move Sewing Lines
Content: Objective Select and move Sewing Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Click on the desired Sewing Line. The selected Sewing Line is highlighted and the dotted line appears to indicate its pair. Note: When you click overlapped Sewing Line, you can select the desired one in the pop-up menu. To select multiple Sewing Line at once, click and drag on the 2D window and encompass all Sewing Line to be selected. The Sewing Lines within the marquee box are highlighted. Click and drag the selected Sewing Lines to move their position.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for selecting and moving sewing lines within the 2D/3D toolbar of the sewing edit menu.

Title: Check Sewing Length
Content: Objective Check significant difference in Sewing Line lengths. You can check unintended Sewing Line length difference made during the garment making process. Location Main Menu Sewing Check Sewing Length 2D Toolbar Check Sewing Length Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Check Sewing Length 2D Toolbar Check Sewing Length The Sewing Lines with length difference greater than 5mm are bolded and highlighted in red.
ContentDescription: This web page allows users to identify and review significant discrepancies in Sewing Line lengths during garment production, highlighting any differences greater than 5mm for easy reference.

Title: Delete Sewing
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Sewing Lines. Location 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Tool Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Delete Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Tool Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Delete Sewing Note: You can also select it and hit the Delete key on the keyboard to delete the Sewing Line.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for efficiently deleting unnecessary sewing lines using the 2D/3D Toolbar and right-click options in the Edit Sewing Tool.

Title: Reverse Sewing
Content: Objective Reverse Directional Notches of Sewing Lines. Location 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Reverse Sewing (Ctrl + B) Operation Select the Sewing Lines to be reversed. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Reverse Sewing (Ctrl + B) The Sewing Lines' Directional Notches are reversed.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for reversing the directional notches of sewing lines using the 2D/3D toolbar and right-click pop-up menu in your design software.

Title: Edit Sewing Line Length
Content: Objective Adjust Sewing Line length. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Click and drag either end point of the Sewing Line to adjust its length. Note: While clicking and dragging the end of the Sewing Line in the 2D Window, right-click and type in the Distance Moved or Total Length in the Moving Distance window.
ContentDescription: "Adjust the length of the Sewing Line easily by clicking and dragging its endpoints in the 2D window or entering specific measurements for precise modifications."

Title: Activate/Deactivate Sewing Lines
Content: Objective Activate or deactivate Sewing Lines as needed. Use this function when Sewing Lines should be applied after the garment is draped, such as the back slits for a men's jacket. Location 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) Deactivated Sewing Lines appear in white in the 2D and the 3D window.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for activating or deactivating Sewing Lines in garment design, allowing users to manage their visibility and application effectively within 2D and 3D views.

Title: Add Point to Pattern on Start/End
Content: Objective Add point to Pattern outline on start or end point of a Sewing line. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right click on the Sewing Line. The right click pop-up menu appears. At your need, add point to Pattern outline on either the start or the end point of the selected Sewing Line. The point is added respective to the chosen option. Note: The point is added to the Pattern outline where the selected Sewing Line is placed on. The same procedure can be repeated to add a point to the pattern outline where the other half of the sewing line is placed
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding points to the Pattern outline at the start or end of a Sewing line using the 2D Toolbar in the Sewing Edit menu.

Title: Symmetrical 3D State (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Easily apply the simulation of pattern to its symmetric pattern. Steps 1. This feature only applies to patterns with Symmetrized set. 2. In the 3D window, right-click on a pattern that is set to symmetrically. 3. Select the Symmetric Arrangement menu from the right-click pop-up menu. End Result The selected pattern is transformed into a simulated version of the opposite Symmetric pattern and is symmetrically arranged relative to the origin of the grid.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a straightforward guide on how to simulate and arrange symmetric patterns in a 3D environment for enhanced visual symmetry.

Title: Delete Bounding Voulme
Content: Objective Delete Bounding Volume no longer in need. Note: When deleting Bounding Volume, be aware that all corresponding Arrangement Points also get deleted from the 3D window. Select the Arrangement Points and assign them to another Bounding Volume to avoid any loss. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Delete Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Delete Selected Bounding Volume is now being deleted from the Bounding Volume list and the 3D window. Note: Selecting a Bounding Volume in the 3D window and pressing Delete key on keyboard also allows to delete it.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidelines for safely deleting a Bounding Volume and managing associated Arrangement Points in the Avatar Editor.

Title: Rearrange Bounding Volume: Fit to Avatar
Content: Objective Rearrange Bounding Volume according to current avatar size when changing its pose or loading another avatar joints. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Fit to Avatar (All) Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Fit to Avatar (All) Bounding Volume is now being fitted to the new avatar's joints.
ContentDescription: This web page allows users to dynamically adjust the bounding volume to match the current avatar's size and pose for optimal alignment and interaction.

Title: Add Arrangement Point
Content: Objective Add new Arrangement Point on the Bound Volume as needed. Note: Without corresponding Bounding Volume, the Arrangement Point is invisible. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Add Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Add A new arrangement point called "Arrangement Point" is now being created at the bottom of the A-Point list in the Arrangement tab, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set details for Arrangement Point. Name Changes the name of the Arrangement Point. Arrangement Arrangement BV Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point to be placed. X Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction The direction in which the Pattern wrapped around the Avatar. Note: Symmetric Arrangement Point Setting Name the Arrangement Point with an underscore and location (R for right and L for left) at the end of the name to set Symmetric Arrangement Point. The name must be the same as the name before the underscore and the alphabet. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default (ver3.0). _R _L Follow the indicated steps below to save the Avatar and Arrangement Points, and reload to apply the setting. Light-blue outer line appears around the Symmetric Arrangement Point. Save Avatar: Main Menu File Save as Avatar Save Arrangement Point: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Save
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for adding and configuring new Arrangement Points within the Avatar Editor, ensuring proper placement and visibility in relation to the Bounding Volume.

Title: Open/Save Arrangement Point
Content: Objective Save newly created Arrangement Point, and open and use previously saved Arrangement Points. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Open /Save Operation Open 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Open Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click Open to load. Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Save Save File window appears. 2. Select the desired location to store. 3. Enter the desired file name and click "Save". An .arr file will now be created.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for saving newly created Arrangement Points and accessing previously saved files within the Avatar Editor.

Title: Add Bounding Voulme
Content: Objective Add a Bounding Volume to add arrangement points. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Add Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Add A new Bounding Volume called "Pan" is now being created at the bottom of the Bounding Volume list, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set details for Bounding Volume. Board Check the list of currently added layouts and edit the properties of the layout by selecting the desired item. Name Changes the name of the Bounding Volume. Arrangement BV Joint Name 0 Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume starts. Joint Name 1 Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume ends. Shape (ver MD10) Depending on the shape of the Avatar, the Bounding Volume is set to the Cylinder and Cuboid. Height Sets the height of the Bounding Volume. Length X Adjusts the circumference of the left and right radii of the Bounding Volume. Length Y Adjusts the circumference of the top and bottom radii of the Bounding Volume. Round Corner (ver MD10) It is active only when the Bounding Volume type is set to Cuboid. Adjust the radius of each corner. Hands/Feet If this option is activated, the length of the Bounding Volume is adjusted to the avatar's hands and feet. The moment you click that option, the entire Bounding Volume is refreshed. Note: If the order below/above the joint points is reversed, the left and right sides are flipped when arranging the Pattern.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a concise guide for adding and customizing a new Bounding Volume named "Pan" in the Avatar Editor, enabling users to define arrangement points and adjust layout properties effectively.

Title: Open/Save Bounding Volume
Content: Objective Save newly created Bounding Volume, open and use previously saved Arrangement Points. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Open / Save Operation Open Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Open Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click Open to load. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Save Save File window appears. Select the desired location to store. Enter the desired file name and click Save. A .pan file is now being created.
ContentDescription: This web page provides users with the functionality to save newly created Bounding Volumes and access previously saved Arrangement Points within the Avatar Editor.

Title: Reset Bounding Volumes (ver4.2.0)
Content: Objective Reset Bounding Volumes to the original placement after adjustments. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes Bounding Volumes are replaced with their original placements.
ContentDescription: "Reset bounding volumes to their original placements in the Avatar Editor for precise adjustments and arrangements."

Title: Delete Arrangement Point
Content: Objective Delete Arrangement Points no longer in need. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Delete Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Delete Selected Arrangement Point is now being deleted from the Arrangement Point list and the 3D window.
ContentDescription: This web page facilitates the deletion of unnecessary arrangement points from the Avatar Editor's main menu, ensuring a streamlined and organized editing experience.

Title: Superimpose
Content: Objective Arrange a newly sewn Pattern onto its corresponding Pattern. This function is helpful when arranging facings, linings, cuffs, collars and other pieces where they need to be arranged directly laying on another. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Superimpose (Over) / Superimpose (Under) / Superimpose (Side) Operation Using the sewing tools, sew a new Pattern to an existing Pattern that is being draped. Follow the indicated guidelines below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Superimpose (Over) / Superimpose (Under) / Superimpose (Side) The selected Pattern is now being arranged accordingly. Note: This function only applies to Patterns that are already being sewn together.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on how to superimpose newly sewn patterns onto existing ones using the 3D Toolbar and right-click pop-up menu for precise arrangement of facings, linings, cuffs, collars, and other garment pieces.
